status.comment: Opt-in methodology and reference runtime; installation never selects or starts a campaign.

p.SELECTION: ZAP is a draft successor methodology for campaigns with interactive initial design and extended autonomous execution. Loading or installing this package does not select it for a campaign, replace a multi-user-planning context, activate a mandate, or authorize execution. An existing central coordinator remains authoritative until the owner explicitly selects a supported migration.

p.SCOPED-READING: For ZAP design work, use zap-draft and read ZAP-METHODOLOGY.xml. For store import, migration and inspection, use zap-state and its command contract. For explicitly configured execution, trusted control or backend serving, use zap-run and the public runtime, CLI and backend contracts. Read ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER.xml for data architecture or integration design. The research map is rationale, not a runtime instruction dependency. Workers with explicit packets keep their packet scope; this flow does not make them central coordinators.

p.CAPABILITIES: The package contains research, planned methodology and a bounded Python reference implementation with deterministic replay, trusted owner/coordinator control, source capture, automatic coordination, durable subprocess transport and an authenticated graph backend. Every action still requires its implemented policy, authority and evidence checks. Import and installation remain inert; only an explicit trust configuration, charter activation and runtime command can start work. The package provides data for a future canvas but no UI application or IDE.

p.CANON: Methodology: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root. Data and future viewer: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root. Runtime: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUNTIME#root. Public CLI, backend and embedding API: vibevm/vibespecs/flows/zap/ZAP-CLI.md, ZAP-BACKEND-API.md and ZAP-PYTHON-API.md. Research: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/research/zap/IDEA-MAP#root.
